magic-kingdom: The whole park sits on a second storey: underneath runs the 'utilidor' tunnel network, so the street you walk to the castle is technically the roof.
epcot: Spaceship Earth never drips on the queue — the giant sphere swallows rainwater through hidden gutters and pipes it away underground.
hollywood-studios: The Tower of Terror doesn't drop you — it pulls you down faster than gravity, which is why your stomach files a complaint.
animal-kingdom: This is the largest theme park on the planet by area, and most of that land belongs to the animals, not the rides.
disneyland: The only park Walt Disney ever walked himself — and on opening day in 1955 a plumbers' strike meant a choice between toilets and drinking fountains. Toilets won.
california-adventure: You are strolling on Disneyland's original parking lot — the tram spaces got upgraded to a whole second park.
universal-studios-florida: When it opened in 1990 this was a working film studio — real productions shot here between the rides.
islands-of-adventure: The Incredible Hulk coaster launches you uphill from 0 to highway speed in about two seconds — tunnel included.
epic-universe: Orlando's first all-new major theme park in over 25 years — you're visiting a piece of theme-park history while the paint is still fresh.
universal-studios-hollywood: The Studio Tour has been running since 1964 — the tram was the whole park before a single ride existed.
disneyland-paris: The most-visited theme park in all of Europe — more people pass these gates each year than visit the Eiffel Tower.
walt-disney-studios-paris: The smallest Disney park in the world — currently in the middle of the biggest expansion in its history.
tokyo-disneyland: Not actually owned by Disney — Japan's Oriental Land Company runs it, and its exclusive popcorn-bucket culture is a national collecting sport.
tokyo-disneysea: Widely reported as the most expensive theme park ever built — roughly four billion dollars, and every yen is visible from the harbour.
hong-kong-disneyland: The park was laid out with feng shui masters — even the entrance angle was adjusted to let good fortune flow in.
shanghai-disneyland: The Enchanted Storybook Castle is the tallest and largest Disney castle ever built — every earlier castle looks up to it.
knotts-berry-farm: America's oldest theme park started as an actual berry farm — the boysenberry was popularised right here, next to a fried-chicken stand.
six-flags-magic-mountain: More roller coasters than any other park on Earth — this is the world-record holder you're pacing yourself through.
busch-gardens-tampa: Half theme park, half accredited zoo — you can watch giraffes and zebras roam a Serengeti plain from a steam train between coasters.
seaworld-orlando: The coasters here are built over and around real marine habitats — you can go from a hypercoaster to a penguin colony in five minutes.
cedar-point: Operating since 1870 on a Lake Erie peninsula — one of the oldest amusement parks in America and self-declared roller coaster capital of the world.
kings-island: The Beast has been the longest wooden roller coaster on Earth since 1979 — it disappears into its own private forest.
six-flags-great-adventure: The drive-through safari next door makes this one of the largest theme-park properties anywhere — lions live within earshot of the coasters.
canadas-wonderland: Canada's largest theme park — and yes, that mountain at the front gate is hollow, with a ride hiding inside it.
hersheypark: Milton Hershey built this park in 1906 so his chocolate-factory workers had somewhere fun to spend Sundays. The chocolate still funds a school today.
dollywood: Co-owned by Dolly Parton — and home to a bald-eagle sanctuary, so the national bird literally lives at the park.
busch-gardens-williamsburg: Routinely voted the most beautiful theme park in the world — the coasters are landscaped like a European garden because it is one.
seaworld-san-diego: The original SeaWorld — it opened in 1964 on Mission Bay before the Orlando and San Antonio parks were even sketches.
europa-park: Germany's largest theme park is run by the Mack family — who have been building rides since 1780, before roller coasters had loops, brakes, or fans.
efteling: Open since 1952 — this fairy-tale forest is older than Disneyland and grew from a single storybook wood into a world-class park.
alton-towers: Built in the gardens of a real Gothic stately home — rides can't rise above the treetops, so the big coasters dig into the ground instead.
thorpe-park: An island of thrills built on a flooded gravel pit — the lake surrounding you used to be the quarry floor.
portaventura: Spain's most-visited theme park — Shambhala's camelback hills were among the tallest in Europe when they went up.
phantasialand: Squeezed into an old quarry town, this park packs record-setting coasters into one of the tightest, most intricately themed footprints on Earth.
parc-asterix: France's cheeky Gallic answer to the castle parks — by Toutatis, the coasters here hit some of the fastest speeds in the country.
liseberg: Gothenburg's garden park has run since 1923 — and its wooden coaster Balder keeps winning best-in-world polls against rides three times its size.
six-flags-over-texas: The original Six Flags, opened 1961 — the name counts the six nations whose flags have flown over Texas.
six-flags-fiesta-texas: Built inside a limestone quarry — coasters dive straight off the hundred-foot quarry walls that surround the park.
six-flags-over-georgia: The second Six Flags ever built — open since 1967, with wooden coasters that generations of Atlanta kids measured themselves against.
six-flags-great-america: American Eagle is one of the tallest, fastest racing wooden coasters ever constructed — two trains, one finish line, since 1981.
six-flags-new-england: Superman The Ride has topped world's-best-coaster polls for years — a river-side legend hiding in New England.
six-flags-discovery-kingdom: One of the very few places on Earth where roller coasters share an address with dolphins, sharks and a butterfly habitat.
six-flags-st-louis: Opened in 1971 as the third of the three original Six Flags parks — the Ozark foothills do half the landscaping.
carowinds: The park straddles the North Carolina–South Carolina state line — you can stand in a queue with one foot in each state.
kings-dominion: That's a one-third-scale Eiffel Tower at the centre of the park — Paris via Virginia, with a coaster skyline attached.
dorney-park: Entertaining Pennsylvania since 1884 — one of the oldest operating amusement parks in the United States.
worlds-of-fun: The whole park is themed on Jules Verne's 'Around the World in 80 Days' — you're circumnavigating the globe between coasters.
valleyfair: Minnesota's largest amusement park — and the 'fair' half of the name that later merged into 'Cedar Fair' itself.
michigans-adventure: Michigan's largest park, and Shivering Timbers is one of the longest wooden coasters ever built — a mile-plus of lake-country lumber.
seaworld-san-antonio: The largest of the three SeaWorld parks by area — Texas-sized, as required by local law and custom.
silver-dollar-city: The park literally began as entertainment for the queue of Marvel Cave — an entire theme park grew on top of a cavern you can still tour.
holiday-world: The first park in the world to hand out free soft drinks and free sunscreen to every guest — hospitality as a competitive sport.
kennywood: A National Historic Landmark, open since 1898 — several of its wooden coasters are more than a century old and still running daily.
lagoon: Family-run in Utah since 1886 — and Cannibal's beyond-vertical drop is one of the steepest ever built anywhere.
legoland-florida: Built on the grounds of Cypress Gardens, Florida's very first theme park — the historic botanical gardens still bloom inside.
legoland-california: The first LEGOLAND outside Europe — Miniland USA alone stacks tens of millions of real bricks.
universal-studios-japan: Osaka got Super Nintendo World before anywhere else on Earth — Mario's first theme-park address is right here.
gardaland: Italy's largest theme park sits on the shore of Lake Garda — coasters with an actual lake-and-mountains backdrop.
heide-park: Northern Germany's largest park — Colossos is one of the tallest, fastest wooden coasters ever raised in Europe.
legoland-windsor: The park sits just up the hill from Windsor Castle — the bricks have royal neighbours.
chessington: It opened as Chessington Zoo in 1931 — the animals held the site for decades before the first coaster moved in.
toverland: 'Toverland' is Dutch for 'magic land' — and nearly half the park is indoors, so the magic is officially weatherproof.
futuroscope: France's park of the future, open since 1987 — it grew from cutting-edge cinema experiments, not coasters, and still feels like science fiction.
everland: South Korea's largest theme park — T Express drops at 77 degrees, one of the steepest wooden coaster descents in the world.
lotte-world: Holder of the Guinness World Record for the largest indoor theme park on Earth — rain has never cancelled a single ride day.
